questions.question: What security risk occurs when external links open with target="_blank" without rel="noopener"?
questions.hint: The opened page can manipulate the opener window.
questions.explanation: Reverse Tabnabbing allows the newly opened tab to access window.opener and redirect the original page to a phishing site.

questions.question: What is the primary defense against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) when rendering user input in HTML?
options: Escaping and encoding HTML entities (like <, >, &, ") before rendering
questions.hint: HTML entity encoding converts executable characters into harmless text.
questions.explanation: Escaping characters into HTML entities prevents user strings from being parsed as executable tags or scripts.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a Content Security Policy (CSP)?
options: To restrict the domains from which scripts, styles, and other resources can be loaded
To enforce two-factor authentication on passwords
questions.explanation: A Content Security Policy (CSP) restricts where scripts, images, and other assets can load from, preventing unauthorized code execution.

questions.question: Which JavaScript property should be used to display user text safely without parsing HTML tags?
questions.hint: textContent treats all input as plain text.
questions.explanation: textContent sets text content safely without interpreting HTML tags, mitigating XSS risks.

questions.question: What is the role of a hidden CSRF token in an HTML <form>?
options: To authenticate that the form submission was generated by a legitimate session on the site
To remember form fields on refresh
questions.explanation: A CSRF token validates that the form request came from an authenticated user on the authentic site, preventing forged requests.
